To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have characterized the five NFU genes from Arabidopsis, and have demonstrated that NFU proteins exist in two classes: a mitochondrial type, and a new class of plastid NFU proteins.
Arabidopsis thalia has two distinct NFU proteins localized to mitochondria and plastid.
we identified and characterized two distinct classes of NFU proteins in plants, one class being specific to the plant lineage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of NFU genes and their encoded proteins from Arabidopsis.
the characterization of the Arabidopsis thalia NFU genes and the study of the role of NFU-like proteins on Fe-S cluster biogeneration.
the study of Fe-S cluster biosynthesis in plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NFU proteins are part of the Fe-S cluster assembly machinery in plants.
NFU-like proteins are part of the Fe-S cluster assembly machinery in both plant mitochondria and chloroplasts.
NFU1 and/or NFU2 proteins are involved in Fe-S cluster assembly in plastids, and NFU4 is involved in Fe-S biogenesis in mitochondria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are two distinct Fe-S assembly machineris, one in mitochondria and one in plastids, with the latter being more complex than the former.
the mitochondrial NFU proteins are more related with the yeast Nfu1p, while the plastidial NFU proteins are unique to plants and more related to the Synechocysti PCC6803 proteins.
NFU1-3 are plastidic proteins that are able to complement a mitochondrial Fe-S cluster deficiency in yeast, and NFU4 and 5 are mitochondrial proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
plants have evolved to have two distinct Fe-S assembly machieries in the plastids and mitochondria.
NFU1 and 2 proteins can functionally replace Nfu1p in yeast.
the NFU proteins have a role in Fe-S cluster biosynthesis in plants.
